before.title: How to Visit Vantara: Tickets, Entry and the Honest Answer
before.contentHtml:
Vantara is not open to the general public. There is no ticket counter, no online booking, no published entry fee and no announced opening date. Vantara's own website says in-person visits are "currently limited and permitted only with approval from regulatory authorities." Every price you have seen online is invented.

That answer will disappoint you, and it is the one thing most pages ranking for this search will not tell you. This guide sets out what the official sources actually say, checked in July 2026, and what you can genuinely visit around Jamnagar instead.

Is Vantara open for public?

No. As of July 2026 Vantara has never been open to general visitors, and no walk-in access exists at any price. The facility was inaugurated on 4 March 2025 and has stayed closed to the public since. Approval sits with regulators, not with Vantara.

The wording matters here, so here it is exactly as Vantara publishes it on its own contact page:

"In-person visits are currently limited and permitted only with approval from regulatory authorities."

Read that carefully. Permission does not come from Vantara. It comes from government regulatory authorities, which means there is no customer-facing request channel at all. No form, no email address for visit requests, no waiting list you can join.

Vantara ticket price and online booking

There is no Vantara ticket price, because there are no tickets. We checked vantara.in and the official Greens Zoological Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre site in July 2026. Neither carries a ticketing page, a booking portal, a fee table or opening hours. Nothing is on sale.

This is worth being blunt about. Search "vantara ticket booking" and you will find pages offering all of the following:

  • "2026 entry fees" in neat tables, adult and child rates
  • Family combo tickets for two adults and two children
  • Student discounts and safari add-ons
  • "Book online" buttons
  • A phone number presented as a ticket enquiry line

None of it is real. Not one of those pages is official, not one cites Vantara, and the numbers do not agree with each other because each site made up its own. Even a major international travel platform lists opening hours for Vantara that do not exist.

If a site asks you to pay for a Vantara ticket, you are being asked to pay for nothing. Do not enter card details.

How to visit Vantara

Access has gone to people brought in through official channels rather than anyone who applied as a tourist. Based on the Supreme Court record and Vantara's own statements, the groups that have been inside fall into a narrow set, and none of them got there by booking.

Who has visitedHow
Regulatory and government officialsOfficial inspection or state visit
Veterinarians and wildlife scientistsProfessional or research invitation
Court-appointed investigatorsStatutory authority
Approved student and institutional groupsProgramme arranged institution to institution
Invited guests and mediaDirect invitation from Vantara
General public and touristsNo route exists

Our recommendation: if you are not in one of the first five rows, do not build a Jamnagar trip around Vantara, and do not pay an agent who claims they can arrange entry. Plan the trip around what is genuinely open, and treat Vantara as something that may become visitable later.

When will Vantara open for public?

No opening date has been announced, and nobody publishing one has a source for it. There is, though, one genuine reason to think partial public access is at least being considered, and it comes from the Supreme Court of India rather than from a travel blog or a press release.

In its order of 15 September 2025 the Court accepted the report of a Special Investigation Team headed by former Supreme Court judge Jasti Chelameswar. Among the SIT's recommendations was that some portions of the rescue centres and the elephant camp "may be opened for public access," on the reasoning that it would improve transparency.

That is a recommendation, not a decision. It has not been implemented, no timeline was attached, and nothing on any official Vantara channel has followed it. Treat it as the most credible signal available, and nothing more.

One date is worth watching. On 27 May 2026 the Court directed India's CITES Management Authority to prepare a stricter import-permit procedure within three months, which puts a deadline around late August 2026. Announcements about Vantara have tended to cluster around court dates.

How to spot a fake Vantara ticket page

This search has attracted an unusual amount of invented content, more than almost any Indian attraction we have looked at, so here is a practical filter you can apply in about ten seconds. Any page that fails these five checks is guessing, no matter how official the layout looks.

  1. Does it quote an exact entry fee? No official fee exists. A specific number is the single clearest tell.
  2. Does it link to vantara.in for the price? The official site has no price to link to, so the citation will be missing or point somewhere else.
  3. Does it give opening hours? None are published. Invented hours are common, including on large booking platforms.
  4. Does it give an opening date? None has been announced.
  5. Is the domain a Vantara lookalike? Several ranking sites use domains built from the word Vantara to look official. The only official site is vantara.in.

The prices you find are not stale information that used to be right. They were never right.

Where is Vantara in Jamnagar?

Vantara sits inside the Reliance complex at Motikhavdi, in Jamnagar district, Gujarat, in western India. The associated Greens Zoological Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre is at Padana in the same district. Neither location has a visitor gate, so the addresses are context rather than directions.

Jamnagar itself is straightforward to reach if you are travelling for other reasons:

  • By air: Jamnagar has its own airport with domestic connections.
  • By train: Jamnagar is on the Western Railway network.
  • By road: roughly two hours from Rajkot, and about five to six hours from Ahmedabad.

What is Vantara?

Vantara, meaning "Star of the Forest", is an animal rescue, care and rehabilitation programme established by Anant Ambani and Reliance in Jamnagar. It is a working veterinary and rehabilitation operation rather than a zoo or a safari park, which is the root of why public access is limited.

Scale, from figures recorded in the Supreme Court's September 2025 order:

MeasureFigure
Animals in care40,633
Elephants275
Capacity approved by the Central Zoo Authority75,000

The animals are largely rescued, seized or retired, including elephants, big cats and reptiles, supported by a large veterinary hospital. Many are recovering from injury or long-term neglect, which is a real argument against opening the gates to daily crowds.

Why regulators control access

Vantara has been through sustained legal and international scrutiny since 2025, and the outcome of it explains why entry is a regulator's decision rather than a booking. This is the short factual version, taken from the court record and the CITES papers, with both linked at the end.

The Supreme Court's SIT reported in September 2025 that it found no violation of India's Wildlife Protection Act, the zoo rules, customs law or CITES, and recorded animal deaths as attributable to natural causes. The Court accepted that report and, in March 2026 and again in May 2026, declined to order fresh investigations.

Separately, in November 2025 the CITES Secretariat reported that two export permits covering eight chimpanzees had been confirmed as forgeries by Cameroon's authorities, and that India's checks had generally not gone beyond confirming an export permit existed. That is a finding about paperwork at the exporting end, and it is why the Court ordered a tighter permit procedure in May 2026.

The practical takeaway for a visitor is simple: access decisions sit with regulators precisely because the facility is under regulatory supervision. That is unlikely to change quickly.

What you can actually visit near Jamnagar

If you are already travelling to this corner of Gujarat, these places are genuinely open, ticketed where relevant, and close enough to Jamnagar to build a day around. Consider this the honest substitute for the Vantara visit you came here looking for.

  • Marine National Park, Gulf of Kachchh. India's first marine national park, reachable from Jamnagar, best at low tide for coral and birdlife.
  • Lakhota Lake and Lakhota Museum, in the middle of Jamnagar city, an easy couple of hours.
  • Barda Wildlife Sanctuary, south of the city, hill forest with leopard and a range of birds.
  • Khijadiya Bird Sanctuary, strong in winter for migratory waterbirds.

Further afield, our guides to the Bhuj to Dholavira road trip and Statue of Unity ticket prices cover the two Gujarat trips people most often pair with a western Gujarat visit. If you are interested in how restricted-access sites in India handle visitor permission, our guide to getting permission to visit ISRO Sriharikota covers a place that does have a real application route.

Frequently asked questions

Is Vantara open to the public in 2026?

No. Vantara has not opened to general visitors at any point since its inauguration on 4 March 2025, and it remains closed in July 2026. Its official contact page states that in-person visits are limited and permitted only with approval from regulatory authorities.

How much is a Vantara ticket?

There is no ticket and no price. Neither vantara.in nor the official Greens Zoological Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre site publishes an entry fee, a booking system or opening hours. Any specific figure you find, including tables labelled 2026 entry fees, was invented by that website.

Can we visit Vantara?

Not as a member of the public. Access has been limited to officials, veterinary and scientific professionals, court-appointed investigators, approved institutional groups and invited guests. There is no public application route, no waiting list, and no agent who can legitimately arrange entry for a tourist.

How can I get permission to visit Vantara?

There is no process open to individuals. Permission rests with regulatory authorities rather than with Vantara itself, so there is nobody to apply to as a tourist. Institutions sometimes arrange visits directly, but that route is not available to the general public.

Is Vantara a zoo?

No. It is a rescue and rehabilitation centre for animals that are injured, seized or retired, built around a large veterinary hospital. The Central Zoo Authority regulates it, which is why the word zoo appears in official paperwork, but it does not operate as a public zoo.

Where is Vantara located?

Vantara is at Motikhavdi in Jamnagar district, Gujarat, inside the Reliance complex. The associated Greens Zoological Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre is at Padana in the same district. Jamnagar has its own airport and sits on the Western Railway network.

When will Vantara open for the public?

No date has been announced. The Supreme Court's Special Investigation Team recommended in September 2025 that parts of the site might be opened for public access to improve transparency, but that recommendation has not been implemented and carried no timeline.

Sources

  • Vantara official site and contact page, vantara.in, checked July 2026
  • Greens Zoological Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre, gzrrc.in
  • Supreme Court of India order, C.R. Jaya Sukin v. Union of India, W.P.(C) 783/2025, order dated 15 September 2025
  • CITES Standing Committee document SC79 Doc. 6.3.4, November 2025
  • Supreme Court order of 27 May 2026 on import-permit procedure, as reported by Bar and Bench
  • Inauguration, News On Air, March 2025

This is a research guide built from official sources and court records. We have not visited Vantara, because no public route exists to do so. Access rules can change: check vantara.in before making any plan, and treat any third party selling tickets as illegitimate.
before.metaTitle: Vantara Ticket Price and Entry: Is It Open to the Public?
before.metaDescription: Vantara is not open to the public and has no tickets, no booking and no published entry fee. What the official site and the court record actually say, checked July 2026.

before.reasoning: Rewrite and expansion of the site's biggest page-2 opportunity. GSC (22 Apr to 21 Jul 2026) shows 171 Vantara queries carrying 2,248 impressions against only 7 clicks, at an average position of 18.5. The cluster splits in a revealing way: transactional queries (vantara ticket booking 308 impressions, vantara ticket 151, vantara entry fees 128, 1,263 in total) already rank 9 to 13, while the questions this page answers best (is vantara open for public 180, can we visit vantara 102, is vantara open to public 82, 440 in total) sit at 28 to 35. The existing page was honest but only 697 words of body, too thin to hold either set. Central fact verified personally against the primary source rather than taken from the research agent: vantara.in's own contact-page FAQ answers 'Is Vantara open to visitors?' with 'In-person visits are currently limited and permitted only with approval from regulatory authorities.' Confirmed no ticketing page, no fee, no opening hours and no opening date exist on vantara.in or gzrrc.in. Every competitor ranking for these queries publishes fabricated entry fees, family combo tickets and booking buttons for a facility with no ticketing whatsoever, and a major international travel platform lists invented opening hours. Original elements: (1) a five-point test for spotting a fabricated Vantara ticket page, which nobody has written and which is the practical thing a searcher needs; (2) the Supreme Court SIT's actual recommendation of September 2025 that parts of the site 'may be opened for public access', reported accurately as an unimplemented recommendation rather than as an opening date; (3) a table of who has genuinely been admitted and by what route, ending with the honest row that no route exists for the public; (4) the late-August 2026 CITES import-permit SOP deadline as the next real date to watch. Deliberately excluded: any price, any booking link, any opening date, the phone number several sites present as a ticket line (describing the pattern without amplifying the number), and the query 'vantara kanhol', which 60 impressions notwithstanding has no verifiable referent in any official, CZA or news source. Also excluded is the separate Telangana night safari MoU, which is a different facility in a different state and would mislead. The weaker duplicate vantara-jamnagar-complete-visitor-guide2025 (331 impressions, position 35.3, year in slug) 301s here.
